title: Tech Note: 4D and Google Charts API - Part 2
author: Jean-Jacques BLEU, 4D Developer
featured_technology: Google Charts API / Visualization library (corechart, gauge, table packages)
4D Web Area object for in-app chart rendering (no Web Server required)
Cached HTML templates for repeated chart rendering

historical_commentary.text: This note's headline achievement — rendering Google Charts inside a 4D Web Area entirely offline from 4D's own Web Server, driven by real 4D database data — remains a broadly valid architecture today; Web Areas and third-party JS charting libraries are still commonly combined this way. The specific mechanism for injecting 4D data into the HTML template, 4D's classic PROCESS 4D TAGS command with #4DHTML/#4DTEXT/#4DIF tags, is a legacy templating technique that has been effectively superseded by more modern approaches: building JSON payloads with 4D's native JSON commands and injecting them via WA Evaluate JavaScript or a lightweight REST/ORDA-backed endpoint, which is more maintainable and less coupled to 4D's older tag-substitution engine.
related_updates: 4D's native JSON commands (JSON Stringify/Parse) combined with WA Evaluate JavaScript are now a more common way to feed data into a Web Area's embedded JavaScript than PROCESS 4D TAGS templating
4D's REST server (built on ORDA, v16 R5+, 2017) can serve chart-ready JSON data without a hand-rolled Web Server/PROCESS 4D TAGS pipeline
